entities.summary: Alcetas was the younger brother of Perdiccas and the son of Orontes from Orestis. He was first mentioned as one of Alexander the Great's generals in his Indian expedition, which took place between 327 and 326 BCE. This expedition marked a significant turning point in the history of the ancient world, as it showcased Alexander's military prowess and expanded his empire. The legacy of Alcetas' participation in this expedition can be seen in the continued influence of Alexander's successors, who went on to shape the course of history in their own right. Alcetas' brother, Perdiccas, would go on to become one of the most powerful men in Alexander's empire, while the expedition itself laid the groundwork for the Hellenistic period. The Indian subcontinent, which was conquered by Alexander's forces, would remain a region of strategic importance for centuries to come. As a result, Alcetas' role in this expedition continues to be studied by historians today.
